text:
Paul Cotter has a Stanley Cup ring from Vegas, 60 hits in 18 games, and four goals on 13 shots for Vancouver. That last number is the one to watch, because it won't hold. A 30.8% shooting percentage is the kind of thing that happens to fourth-liners in short bursts.

The rest of the picture is rough. The Canucks have taken just 32% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 11 points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season said offense isn't his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agrees that his value, if it's there, isn't in creating chances at five on five. His ice time has dropped by more than two minutes a night over his last ten games, and he hasn't scored in that stretch.

What he brings is speed (faster than 83% of the league by NHL Edge) and physicality. Our range has him at 9 to 17 goals over a full season. On a team that's still deciding what it is, he's a useful energy player who shouldn't be asked to do more than that.
headline: Cotter's goals came early
